unit: Unit 1: Database System Concepts, ER Model & Relational Design

questions.stem: Logical Data Independence ensures that changes to the conceptual schema (such as adding a new entity or attribute) do not require changes to existing external schemas or application programs.
questions.rationale: True. Logical Data Independence is the capacity to change the conceptual schema without having to alter external schemas or existing application programs that do not reference the modified entities. (Key Takeaway: Logical data independence shields external views against conceptual schema expansion.)

questions.stem: In formal ER semantics, what structural constraint characterizes a binary relationship set with cardinality ratio 1:1 and partial participation on both entity sets?

options.text: Each entity in E1 maps to at most one in E2, each in E2 maps to at most one in E1, and entities in either set may exist unassociated
Every entity in E1 must associate with every entity in E2 simultaneously
Entities on either side are forbidden from possessing primary key attributes

questions.rationale: A 1:1 relationship with partial participation on both sides bounds the maximum cardinality to 1 and minimum cardinality to 0 in both directions, meaning relationships are singular and optional for both participating entity sets. (Key Takeaway: 1:1 partial participation bounds associations to at most one and allows unlinked entities.)

questions.module_title: Advanced ER and Extended ER (EER) Concepts
questions.stem: In formal EER theory, Total Specialization dictates that the union of all subclass entity sets must equal the entire superclass entity set ($S = \bigcup_{i} C_i$).
questions.rationale: True. Total specialization (completeness constraint, denoted by a double line) mandates that every entity in the superclass must be a member of at least one subclass, meaning the subclasses completely partition the superclass domain. (Key Takeaway: Total specialization enforces completeness where the superclass equals the union of its subclasses.)

questions.stem: Is the Tuple Relational Calculus (TRC) expression {t | NOT (t in R)} considered a 'Safe' relational calculus expression?
questions.rationale: No. An expression is unsafe if it can evaluate to an infinite relation. Since the complement of relation R contains an infinite number of tuples outside the active domain of the database, {t | NOT (t in R)} is unsafe and prohibited. (Key Takeaway: Unsafe TRC expressions can produce infinite relations and are rejected.)

questions.stem: When mapping an N-ary relationship set ($N > 2$) where all participating entity sets have 'Many' cardinality into a relation, what forms the primary key of the resulting junction table?

options.text: An arbitrarily selected single foreign key from one participating entity
The composite combination of foreign keys referencing all N participating entity sets
Composite keys are forbidden; a surrogate string column must be generated

questions.rationale: When all participating entity sets have Many cardinality in an N-ary relationship, no proper subset of foreign keys can uniquely identify relationship instances. Hence, the primary key must be the composite combination of all N foreign keys. (Key Takeaway: N-ary relationships with Many cardinalities require composite primary keys combining all foreign keys.)

questions.stem: In Relational Algebra, the Division operator (R / S) is the formal algebraic counterpart for queries involving Universal Quantification ('for all').
questions.rationale: True. The relational division operator $R(X, Y) \div S(Y)$ identifies tuples in $X$ that are associated with ALL tuples in $S(Y)$, expressing canonical universal quantification queries (such as 'find customers who bought ALL products'). (Key Takeaway: Relational division formally computes universal quantification queries.)
